MOZAMBIQUE ATTACKS 2021

By: Nicky Troll | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
A brutal ISIS-led attack claims the lives of local and expats in violent attack in northern Mozambique – in an exclusive interview we speak to some of the South African survivors.

Summary:
HOW WE TELL IT:
We focus on the human story, with a strong personal narrative. We hear from Survivors, people on the ground helping with evacuations and one expert for context.

INTERVIEWS:
1. Wesley or Gregory Knox who were there and after hiding their Adrian’s body – carried it onto the evacuation boat in a desperate escape.
WORST CASE SCENARIO WE GE THE MOM – Meryl Knox
2. ISS – Liesl Louw – the attacks escalated over time – there was intelligence that this was coming
3. Benedicta Schall – helped with the evacuation of people on boats. She is in Mozambique.

FOOTAGE
- Some stuff on social media
- BBC Footage from earlier this year (Siniketiwe is finding out if we can use it with a credit on-screen, otherwise AM will get costing from the BBC local peeps)
- Lots of Reuters footage – Nikola has asked Gallo to help get us stuff – last resort we have to get price from Reuters
- Might be able to steal 20 seconds on Fair Use news basis
- Have one clip of militants prepping for attack
- Re-enactment of Adrian Nel story.


Further information:
More than half a million people have fled their homes due to an Islamist insurgency in northern Mozambique, and the violence and humanitarian crisis will worsen without international help according to United Nations officials.

“If nothing is done soon, we won’t have only 535,000 displaced people. We won’t have only 2,000 people killed by the conflict, but tens of thousands,” said Valentin Tapsoba, regional director for the United Nations refugee agency (UNHCR).

WHO
Al-Shabab is how Mozambicans now refer to a shadowy Islamist insurgency that began four years ago in the province - an insurgency that was initially dismissed as a minor distraction in a region that is rich in minerals and focused on reaping the benefits of an international $15bn (£11bn) off-shore gas project.

Today things look very different, with a third of the province's population forced to flee. The US state department has designated the insurgents as a terrorist organisation dubbed "Isis-Mozambique" - a reference to the franchise arrangement that the Islamic State group (IS) is believed to have set up with the local faction.

WHERE
Palma is home to French energy group Total and is a logistics hub for international gas projects worth about $60bn (nearly R900bn) – about 10km from the actual gas project – it is one of the biggest investments in Africa.

OCTOBER 2017
Insurgents staged their first attack in Cabo Delgado province - where oil giants such as Total are involved in big gas projects. 30 armed men launched a dawn raid on three police stations Mocimboa da Praia, port city in the province of Cabo Delgado, a predominantly Muslim region bordering Tanzania.

The group Ahlu Sunnah Wa-Jama (ASWJ) has triggered a humanitarian crisis. It pledged allegiance to Islamic State two years later. The conflict has escalated since, with attacks growing in scale and frequency and the militants regularly taking and holding entire towns. Their tactics have involved burning villages and beheading locals.

AUGUST 2020
They seized the town of Mocimboa da Praia and are still in control.

NOVEMBER / DECEMBER 2020
Dozens of people were reportedly beheaded by Islamic militants in northern Mozambique. Now the beheadings and bloodshed have spread to the town of Palma, taking the bloodshed to another level.

FAST FORWARD 2021
Total said on March 24 it would resume construction of its liquefied natural gas infrastructure after the establishment of the zone. But within hours the attacks began, and nearly 200 expatriates and local officials were told to wait at the Amarula Palma Hotel for boats to ferry them to safety. 43 South Africans were trapped in the horror attack.

Heavily armed rebel forces began attacking Palma in the province of Cabo Delgado in Mozambique,t argeting shops, banks and a military barracks.

Wednesday's attack follows the December attack on the Palma area which led to non-essential Total staff being evacuated from the site. Armed militants moved in on the coastal town that is home to 75 000 people, from three different directions – locals and some 200 workers were forced to flee.

Before the attack the company said security had improved in the area with a 25km protective area around the Afungi site. But according to ISS’ Martin Ewi – the authorities knew of the imminent attack”because there was intelligence that an attack was going to occur at leats for three days before”, but did nothing to prevent it.

Seven people have been confirmed dead – they were killed trying to escape a siege on a hotel.

SOUTH AFRICAN KILLED
Adrian Nel was killed trying to escape. Nel was a commercial diver who had lost his job in South Africa because of the devastating impact of Covid-19.

He moved to Mozambique in January to join his step father and younger half-brother in the construction industry, building workers' accommodation camps in Palma, which has become the hub of a burgeoning gas industry following the offshore discovery of one of the largest natural gas fields in Africa.

A mere three months later, he faced a cruel death, having been shot by militants who had carried out a four-day assault on the town, targeting shops, banks, a military barracks and the Amarula Hotel, where Nel, his father and younger brother had taken refuge along with other expatriates.

His step-father, Gregory, managed to make it out of Palma - though he had to carry the body of their dead son until he was rescued. Her other son was also able to escape. But once they had fled, they had "no army to protect them... it was a matter of, 'run for your life'".

STATUS QUO
The government has yet to re-establish control. On March 27 Total said it was calling off a planned resumption of construction at its $20bn (nearly R300bn) development after the attack.

The town and beaches are strewn with bodies "with heads and without", according to Col Lionel Dyke, whose private security firm, Dyck Advisory Group, is contracted by the Mozambique police in the area.

EVACUATION EFFORTS
Witnesses have described hiding out while waiting to be rescued by boat, on a beach strewn with headless bodies. Marine traffic websites showed a string of vessels around the town, and the port of Pemba to the south, as people tried to escape by any means - cargo vessels, passenger ships, tugs and recreational boats.

RESCUE MISSION
Civilians living and working in the area appeared to be co-ordinating the rescue effort.
"Local suppliers and companies, these guys were heroes of the entire operation. In the wee hours they managed to co-ordinate and reach out to the evacuees on the beach and got them on to boats and got them into safety."
"Where the hell was the support from big companies, from countries?" he asked.

Some tried to escape the hotel in a convoy of vehicles on Friday, aiming for a nearby beach. At least 20 people were reportedly flown to safety in helicopters, but others were ambushed outside the hotel.

FINAL SCRIPT: MOZAMBIQUE ATTACKS

VO: IN MARCH, CABO DELGADO IN NORTHERN MOZAMBIQUE WAS THRUST ONTO THE GLOBAL MEDIA STAGE. NOT FOR THE REGION’S IDYLLIC COASTAL SHORES, BUT RATHER AS THE CENTRE OF A BRUTAL ISLAMIC STATE LED TERROR ATTACK.

DOZEN HAVE BEEN KILLED. MORE THAN 10 000 PEOPLE FLED THE REGION INCLUDING LOCALS, FOREIGNERS AND ABOUT 50 SOUTH AFRICANS.

LINK: ABOUT 100 HEAVILY ARMED INSURGENTS, SOME SAY MANY MORE WENT ON A RAMPAGE – KILLING AND BEHEADING PEOPLE, SPREADING FEAR AS THEY VIOLENTLY CLAIMED CONTROL OF THE TOWN OF PALMA.

VO: PALMA IS A LOGISTICS HUB FOR THE $60 BILLION US DOLLAR INTERNATIONAL LIQUEFIED NATURAL GAS PROJECTS. IT’S JUST 10 KM FROM FRENCH ENERGY GROUP TOTAL’S AFUNGI’S OPERATION – WHICH IS AFRICA’S LARGEST GAS PRODUCTION FACILITY.

THE VIOLENT, CALCULATED PALMA RAID BROKE A THREE-MONTH LULL IN ISLAMIST ATTACKS THAT HAVE PLAGUED THE REGION SINCE 2017.

LIESL: THIS IS AN INSURGENCY THAT IS HOMEGROWN // THIS IS NOT THE ISLAMIC STATE THAT CAME TO MOZAMBIQUE,.

VO: OVER THE YEARS, THESE INSURGENTS HAVE GAINED SUPPORT, EXPLAINS ANALYST LIESL LOUW-VAUDRUN.

LIESL: THE SENTIMENT WAS THAT A LOT OF THE RICHES WOULD THEN JUST GO TO THE ELITE IN MAPUTO AND THAT LOCAL PEOPLE WON'T BENEFIT OF IT. SO THESE ARE ALL SORT OF INGREDIENTS LIKE A TOXIC MIX OF OF ISSUES THAT MADE PEOPLE SYMPATHETIC OR DROVE SOME YOUTH AND YOUNG PEOPLE TO JOIN THESE EXTREMIST.

LINK: THIS STORY IS NOT ABOUT THE TOTAL INSTALLATION AND LACK OF SECURITY FOR LOCAL VILLAGERS AND CONTACTORS – THIS STORY IS ABOUT A FATHER AND TWO SONS STRUGGLING TO SURVIVE AND ESCAPE AND PROTECT THOSE AROUND THEM.

WES: IT'S SOMETHING OUT OF A MOVIE. I'LL TELL YOU, IT STILL DOESN'T FEEL REAL WHAT HAPPENED YOU KNOW , WE WENT UP THERE TO TO BUILD A CAMP, NOT TO GET CAUGHT IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WAR.

VO: WESLEY NEL WORKED AS A CONSTRUCTION SUB-CONTRACTOR IN PALMA ALONGSIDE HIS STEP-FATHER GREG KNOX AND BROTHER ADRIAN NEL.

ADRIAN DIDN’T MAKE IT BACK TO SOUTH AFRICA. HE WAS KILLED TRYING TO ESCAPE THE ATTACK.
THE EVENTS IN THE DAYS LEADING UP TO HIS DEATH WERE CHILLING TO SAY THE LEAST.

WES: WE STARTED TO HEAR GUNFIRE AND MORTARS BEING DROPPED. AND WHEN THAT HAPPENED, EVERYBODY JUST STARTED RUNNING IN ALL DIRECTIONS.

VO BACK IN SOUTH AFRICA, HIS MOTHER MERYL KNOX WAS DESPERATELY TRYING TO MAKE CONTACT WITH THEM.

MERYL: NOBODY ANSWERED THEIR CELL PHONES. AND I KNEW THIS WASN'T GOING TO BE GOOD.

VO: EVENTUALLY HER HUSBAND CONTACTED HER VIA SATELLITE PHONE ON THE WEDNESDAY NIGHT.

MERYL: AND HE TOLD ME THEY WERE ALL SAFE INSIDE THE AMARULA AND PLANS WERE BEING MADE TO HAVE THEM EVACUATED.

VO: CLOSE TO 200 SUB-CONTRACTORS AND LOCALS FLED TO THE AMARULA HOTEL. WHILE IT HAD A SECURE FENCE AND SOME SECURITY, THE GROUP WAS PAINFULLY AWARE THAT THE MILITANTS WERE NEARBY, EXPLAINS WESLEY.

WES: WHEN WE STARTED GETTING SHOT AT FROM THE ROAD AND HAD TO KEEP OUR HEADS DOWN, THAT'S WHEN WE KNEW IT WAS REAL.

VO: WESLEY RECORDED THIS VIDEO CLIP AT THE AMARULA HOTEL - THAT’S HIS BROTHER ADRIAN TAKING COVER. LISTEN AS SHOTS ARE FIRED AT THE BUILDING.

UPSOUND GUNFIRE
THE THREAT WAS REAL - AND HAD BEEN MOUNTING FOR SOME TIME WITH ATTACKS IN SURROUNDING AREAS, EXPLAINS LOUW-VAUDRUN.

LIESL: PEOPLE FLED TO THE CITY AND SOME OF THESE INSURGENTS // INFILTRATED THEM, HID THEIR WEAPONS, AND THEY WENT INTO THE TOWN. AND FROM THERE, THEY LAUNCHED THESE MASSIVE ATTACKS. PEOPLE WERE SLAUGHTERED

VO THERE WERE WITNESS ACCOUNTS OF BODIES STREWN ACROSS THE TOWN, SOME INTACT, SOME BUTCHERED, SOME DECAPITATED - LEFT OUT ON THE ROADS FOR ALL TO SEE.

LINK: WEDNESDAY HAD GONE, THURSDAY AND NOW FRIDAY AND NO ONE HAD COME TO SAVE THEM AND SOUND OF GUNFIRE WAS GETTING CLOSER.

UPSOUND GUNFIRE

WES: IF WE DON'T LEAVE BEFORE SUNSET, WE WILL GET SLAUGHTERED.//WE WERE ON THE PHONE TO ANYBODY AND EVERYBODY WE COULD JUST SAYING IF THEY CAN'T EVACUATE// IF NOT THAT, AT LEAST DROP GUNS FOR US SO WE CAN TRY TO PROTECT OURSELVES, BECAUSE WE SAID TO THEM, WE'RE SITTING DUCKS HERE

VO: THERE WAS INFORMATION THAT THERE COULD BE WEAPONS IN AN ABANDONED CAR JUST OUTSIDE OF THE HOTEL.

OF THE 188 PEOPLE THERE, IT WAS ADRIAN THAT VOLUNTEERED TO TRY AND RETRIEVE THE WEAPONS, WEARING A BULLETPROOF VEST AND HELMET THEY FOUND IN THE HOTEL.

DEREK: UM, BUT YOUR HEART MUST HAVE BEEN RACING WITH. YEAH.
WES: I MEAN, FOR HIM TO TO RUN OUT // YOU DON'T KNOW IF THERE'S INSURGENTS RIGHT THERE. UM SO HE WAS BRAVE.

VO: ON HIS FIRST ATTEMPT, THE CAR ALARM WAS ACTIVATED, HE RECOVERED A MILITARY BAG, BUT NO GUN.

UPSOUND - ADRIAN - COME BACK

VO: ADRIAN WENT BACK AND FORTH THREE TIMES, THE LAST TRIP HE WAS ACCOMPANIED BY A HOTEL UNARMED SECURITY GUARD.

WES: THEY FOUND THE GUN, BROUGHT IT BACK. AND WE WERE SO HAPPY, YOU KNOW, THAT WAS THAT THAT WAS THERE TO PROTECT US.

VO: BACK HOME MERYL WAS STARTING TO LOSE HOPE OF A SAFE RETURN FOR HER SONS AND HUSBAND.

MERYL: IT SOUNDED LIKE THE INSURGENTS WERE WINNING. AND BY THEN I HAD REPORTS OF THE ARMY RUNNING OFF.

VO: THE GROUP AT THE AMARULA HOTEL HAD DECIDED TO PILE INTO 17 VEHICLES AND MAKE A RUN FOR THE BEACH WHERE THEY COULD BE EVACUATED IN CHOPPERS OPERATED BY DAG, A PRIVATE MILITARY COMPANY.

AS THEY PREPARED FOR THE DAUNTING DRIVE, THE GUNFIRE WAS RELENTLESS.

UPSOUND GUN FIRE

VO: WHILE EVERYONE CRAMMED INTO CARS, ADRIAN, WAS GOING TO DRIVE ONE OF THE CONVOY VEHICLES.

UPSOUND: KEEP YOUR HEAD DOWN HERE - THIS IS GONNA BE THE RIDE OF YOUR LIFE BRO… //

VO: ONE AMBUSH, AND TWO CRASHES LATER, THE CONVOY WAS GETTING SMALLER AND THE TENSION WAS PALPABLE.

WES: THAT'S WHEN THE GUNFIRE THEY THE SECOND AMBUSH HAPPENED AND THEY SHOT US FROM THE SIDE, I DON'T KNOW, BUT LOTS AND LOTS OF ROUNDS. AND I WAS SITTING BEHIND MY BROTHER, // AND HE JUST STARTED SCREAMING AND SHOUTING, I'M HIT, I'M HIT.//

VO: ADRIAN WAS SHOT IN THE ARM AND LEG, BUT HE CARRIED ON DRIVING FOR AS LONG AS HE COULD MANAGE. EVENTUALLY WESLEY TOOK OVER AND ADRIAN WAS MOVED TO THE BACK WITH HIS STEP-FATHER.

WES: I TOLD MY DAD JUST PLEASE SAVE HIM, SAVE HIM. AND I WAS SCREAMING BACK AT HIM THAT I LOVE HIM. I LOVE HIM SO MUCH. AND I PROMISE I'LL LOOK AFTER HIS KIDS AND HIS FAMILY. HE WAS ALREADY GONE. MY DAD WAS SHAKING WE WERE JUST SAYING TO HIM THAT AND WE WE'RE JUST SO, SO SORRY // I TOOK HIS STUFF, TOOK HIS WALLET, I TOOK HIS BANGLE THAT HE ALWAYS HAD AND HIS RING OF FOLDED HIS ARMS. AND I APOLOGIZE TO HIM. I SAID I’M SO SORRY FOR THIS

VO: THEY LEFT ADRIAN’S BODY IN THE CAR AND RAN INTO THE BUSHES TO TAKE COVER AND HIDE FOR THE NIGHT. ONLY 7 CARS IN THE CONVOY MADE IT. AND 6 MORE LIVES WERE LOST ON THE JOURNEY.

WES: I WAS JUST THINKING THAT TO GO BACK TO THE QUARRY, TO GO GET HIM AND BRING HIM WITH ME
DEREK: MUST HAVE BEEN THE LONGEST NIGHT OF YOUR LIFE WAS
WES: ALL I COULD THINK ABOUT WAS, SHOULD WE HAVE STAYED? MAYBE. THEN MY BROTHER WOULDN'T BE DEAD. UM, I DON'T KNOW. I JUST KEEP ON PLAYING THIS THROUGH MY MIND. AND I HAVE FLASHBACKS OF SHOULD WE HAVE MADE A DIFFERENT DECISION? BUT I DON'T KNOW.

VO: THE NEXT MORNING THE DAG CHOPPERS ARRIVED, THEY WOULD BE RESCUED.

MERYL: WE WE JUST VERY THANKFUL TO THEM WITHOUT THEM. I CAN TELL YOU NOW, I WOULD HAVE HAD THREE COFFINS WAITING FOR ME AT THE AIRPORT. // THE DAG GUARDS WENT AND RESCUED THEM AND THEY ACTUALLY WENT BACK TO GO AND RETRIEVE ADRIAN.

VO: ADRIAN NEL IS SURVIVED BY HIS WIFE AND THREE YOUNG CHILDREN.

LIESL: THIS IS VIOLENT EXTREMISM. ALL THE SIGNS WERE THERE. // MOZAMBICAN GOVERNMENT KEPT ON SAYING, NO, THIS IS JUST CRIMINAL ACTIVITY. WE CAN HANDLE IT.

LINK: AND NOW THE BODY COUNT CONTINUES AS THE INSURGENTS IMMERSE THEMSELVES INTO THE COMMUNITY, THE PRIVATE SECURITY HAVE LEFT AND TOTAL HAS SUSPENDED OPERATIONS – AS PALMA IS LEFT DESTROYED AND BURNT TO THE GROUND.

VO: WHILE MORE THAN A THOUSAND PEOPLE WERE EVACUATED BY SEA, MANY ARE STILL TRAPPED. AND WHILE TROOPS WERE DEPLOYED TO CABO DELGADO, MOZAMBIQUE’S ABILITY TO FIGHT THE INSURGENCY HAS LONG BEEN QUESTIONED ACCORDING TO LOUW-VAUDRUN.

LIESL: IT HAS TO BE COMBATED BY AN INTERNATIONAL COALITION BECAUSE THERE'S NO ONE COUNTRY IN ON THE CONTINENT OR EVEN GLOBALLY THAT HAS, YOU KNOW, FOUGHT TERRORISM ALONE. DEFINITELY NOT A WEAK STATE LIKE MOZAMBIQUE.

WES: THE WORLD NEEDS TO DO SOMETHING ABOUT THIS AND THEY NEED TO DO IT FAST. I MANAGED TO GET OUT, BUT HOW MANY PEOPLE ARE STILL IN THE BUSH? THEY ARE HIDING AND I'VE SEEN WHAT THEY HAVE SEEN.



PROMO 1
VO: A SOUTH AFRICAN FAMILY SPEAK TO US AFTER ESCAPING THE BRUTAL ISLAMIC STATE-LED ATTACK IN MOZAMBIQUE.

WES: IT'S SOMETHING OUT OF A MOVIE. I'LL TELL YOU, IT STILL DOESN'T FEEL REAL WHAT HAPPENED

PROMO 2
VO: WE SPEAK TO THE FAMILY OF THE SOUTH AFRICAN KILLED DURING THE VIOLENT ISLAMIC STATE LED INSURGENCE.
WES: I WAS SITTING BEHIND MY BROTHER, // AND HE JUST STARTED SCREAMING AND SHOUTING, I'M HIT, I'M HIT.//

PROMO 3
VO: A SHOCKING STORY OF HEROICS AND SURVIVAL AS A FAMILY RECOUNT THE EVENTS LEADING UP TO THE DEATH OF ADRIAN NEL - HE WAS KILLED IN A BRUTAL ISLAMIC-LED ATTACK IN NORTHERN MOZAMBIQUE.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): A brutal ISIS-led attack claims the lives of local and expats in violent attack in northern Mozambique – in an exclusive interview we speak to some of the South African survivors.
metadata.Summary: HOW WE TELL IT: We focus on the human story, with a strong personal narrative. We hear from Survivors, people on the ground helping with evacuations and one expert for context. INTERVIEWS: 1. Wesley or Gregory Knox who were there and after hiding their Adrian’s body – carried it onto the evacuation boat in a desperate escape. WORST CASE SCENARIO WE GE THE MOM – Meryl Knox 2. ISS – Liesl Louw – the attacks escalated over time – there was intelligence that this was coming 3. Benedicta Schall – helped with the evacuation of people on boats. She is in Mozambique. FOOTAGE - Some stuff on social media - BBC Footage from earlier this year (Siniketiwe is finding out if we can use it with a credit on-screen, otherwise AM will get costing from the BBC local peeps) - Lots of Reuters footage – Nikola has asked Gallo to help get us stuff – last resort we have to get price from Reuters - Might be able to steal 20 seconds on Fair Use news basis - Have one clip of militants prepping for attack - Re-enactment of Adrian Nel story.
metadata.Further information: More than half a million people have fled their homes due to an Islamist insurgency in northern Mozambique, and the violence and humanitarian crisis will worsen without international help according to United Nations officials. “If nothing is done soon, we won’t have only 535,000 displaced people. We won’t have only 2,000 people killed by the conflict, but tens of thousands,” said Valentin Tapsoba, regional director for the United Nations refugee agency (UNHCR). WHO Al-Shabab is how Mozambicans now refer to a shadowy Islamist insurgency that began four years ago in the province - an insurgency that was initially dismissed as a minor distraction in a region that is rich in minerals and focused on reaping the benefits of an international $15bn (£11bn) off-shore gas project. Today things look very different, with a third of the province's population forced to flee. The US state department has designated the insurgents as a terrorist organisation dubbed "Isis-Mozambique" - a reference to the franchise arrangement that the Islamic State group (IS) is believed to have set up with the local faction. WHERE Palma is home to French energy group Total and is a logistics hub for international gas projects worth about $60bn (nearly R900bn) – about 10km from the actual gas project – it is one of the biggest investments in Africa. OCTOBER 2017 Insurgents staged their first attack in Cabo Delgado province - where oil giants such as Total are involved in big gas projects. 30 armed men launched a dawn raid on three police stations Mocimboa da Praia, port city in the province of Cabo Delgado, a predominantly Muslim region bordering Tanzania. The group Ahlu Sunnah Wa-Jama (ASWJ) has triggered a humanitarian crisis. It pledged allegiance to Islamic State two years later. The conflict has escalated since, with attacks growing in scale and frequency and the militants regularly taking and holding entire towns. Their tactics have involved burning villages and beheading locals. AUGUST 2020 They seized the town of Mocimboa da Praia and are still in control. NOVEMBER / DECEMBER 2020 Dozens of people were reportedly beheaded by Islamic militants in northern Mozambique. Now the beheadings and bloodshed have spread to the town of Palma, taking the bloodshed to another level. FAST FORWARD 2021 Total said on March 24 it would resume construction of its liquefied natural gas infrastructure after the establishment of the zone. But within hours the attacks began, and nearly 200 expatriates and local officials were told to wait at the Amarula Palma Hotel for boats to ferry them to safety. 43 South Africans were trapped in the horror attack. Heavily armed rebel forces began attacking Palma in the province of Cabo Delgado in Mozambique,t argeting shops, banks and a military barracks. Wednesday's attack follows the December attack on the Palma area which led to non-essential Total staff being evacuated from the site. Armed militants moved in on the coastal town that is home to 75 000 people, from three different directions – locals and some 200 workers were forced to flee. Before the attack the company said security had improved in the area with a 25km protective area around the Afungi site. But according to ISS’ Martin Ewi – the authorities knew of the imminent attack”because there was intelligence that an attack was going to occur at leats for three days before”, but did nothing to prevent it. Seven people have been confirmed dead – they were killed trying to escape a siege on a hotel. SOUTH AFRICAN KILLED Adrian Nel was killed trying to escape. Nel was a commercial diver who had lost his job in South Africa because of the devastating impact of Covid-19. He moved to Mozambique in January to join his step father and younger half-brother in the construction industry, building workers' accommodation camps in Palma, which has become the hub of a burgeoning gas industry following the offshore discovery of one of the largest natural gas fields in Africa. A mere three months later, he faced a cruel death, having been shot by militants who had carried out a four-day assault on the town, targeting shops, banks, a military barracks and the Amarula Hotel, where Nel, his father and younger brother had taken refuge along with other expatriates. His step-father, Gregory, managed to make it out of Palma - though he had to carry the body of their dead son until he was rescued. Her other son was also able to escape. But once they had fled, they had "no army to protect them... it was a matter of, 'run for your life'". STATUS QUO The government has yet to re-establish control. On March 27 Total said it was calling off a planned resumption of construction at its $20bn (nearly R300bn) development after the attack. The town and beaches are strewn with bodies "with heads and without", according to Col Lionel Dyke, whose private security firm, Dyck Advisory Group, is contracted by the Mozambique police in the area. EVACUATION EFFORTS Witnesses have described hiding out while waiting to be rescued by boat, on a beach strewn with headless bodies. Marine traffic websites showed a string of vessels around the town, and the port of Pemba to the south, as people tried to escape by any means - cargo vessels, passenger ships, tugs and recreational boats. RESCUE MISSION Civilians living and working in the area appeared to be co-ordinating the rescue effort. "Local suppliers and companies, these guys were heroes of the entire operation. In the wee hours they managed to co-ordinate and reach out to the evacuees on the beach and got them on to boats and got them into safety." "Where the hell was the support from big companies, from countries?" he asked. Some tried to escape the hotel in a convoy of vehicles on Friday, aiming for a nearby beach. At least 20 people were reportedly flown to safety in helicopters, but others were ambushed outside the hotel.
